            or record.authorization_refs != p.authorization_refs or record.authorization_refs != (grant.ref,)
            or record.baseline_snapshots != p.baseline_snapshots
            or tuple(b.ref for b in baselines) != record.baseline_snapshots
            or tuple(b.ref for b in resulting) != record.resulting_snapshots
            or record.method_content is not None and record.method_content.schema_ref.method_ref != p.method_ref):
        raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_PACKAGE_BINDING_MISMATCH')
    before = {b.ref.repository_id: {f.path:f.blob_ref.digest for f in b.files} for b in baselines}
    after = {b.ref.repository_id: {f.path:f.blob_ref.digest for f in b.files} for b in resulting}
    if not set(after) <= set(before):
        raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_FOREIGN_REPOSITORY')
    declared = {repo:dict(files) for repo,files in before.items()}
    planned = {(f.repository_id,f.path):f for f in p.resolved_file_manifest}
    touched = set()
    scopes = dict(grant.intent.scope_by_action)
    for change in record.file_changes:
        plan = planned.get((change.repository_id,change.normalized_path))
        if (plan is None or plan.operation != change.operation or plan.rename_from != change.rename_from
                or plan.before_blob_digest != change.before_blob_digest
                or set(plan.proposal_refs) != set(change.proposal_refs)):
            raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_FILE_OUTSIDE_PACKAGE')
        path = change.rename_from if change.operation == 'rename' else change.normalized_path
        destination = change.normalized_path if change.operation == 'rename' else None
        scope = scopes.get('edit_repository')
        if ('edit_repository' not in p.allowed_actions or scope is None
                or not scope.allows_path(change.repository_id,path,change.operation,destination=destination)):
            raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_FILE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE')
        files = declared[change.repository_id]
        for name in {path, change.normalized_path}:
            identity = (change.repository_id,name)
            if identity in touched:
                raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_FILE_CONFLICT')
        touched.add((change.repository_id,path))
        touched.add((change.repository_id,change.normalized_path))
        if change.operation == 'add':
            if path in files:
                raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_BASELINE_MISMATCH')
        elif files.get(path) != change.before_blob_digest:
            raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_BASELINE_MISMATCH')
        if change.operation in ('delete','rename'):
            del files[path]
        if change.operation == 'rename' and destination in files:
            raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_FILE_CONFLICT')
        if change.operation != 'delete':
            files[change.normalized_path] = change.after_blob_digest
        if change.repository_id not in after:
            raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_RESULT_SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED')
    # Full manifest equality catches unreported additions/deletions, including
    # unchanged files silently lost from an allegedly complete resulting tree.
    if any(declared[repo] != files for repo,files in after.items()):
        raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_TREE_DIFF_MISMATCH')
    results = {b.ref.repository_id:b.ref for b in resulting}
    for commit in record.commit_refs:
        snapshot = results.get(commit.repository_id)
        if (snapshot is None or snapshot.commit_id != commit.commit_id or snapshot.tree_digest != commit.tree_digest
                or 'create_local_commit' not in p.allowed_actions):
            raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_COMMIT_BINDING_MISMATCH')
    known_trees = set(record.baseline_snapshots + record.resulting_snapshots)
    requirements = {r.template_id for r in p.acceptance_requirements}
    for check in record.test_evidence:
        if (check.subject_snapshot not in known_trees or check.requirement_id not in requirements
                or 'run_checks' not in p.allowed_actions):
            raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_CHECK_BINDING_MISMATCH')
    for effect in record.effect_observations:
        scope = scopes.get(effect.action)
        if (effect.action not in p.allowed_actions or scope is None
                or not any(limit.action == effect.action and limit.target_id == effect.target_ref.target_id
                    and limit.constraint_digest == effect.target_ref.constraint_digest for limit in scope.effect_limits)):
            raise ReferenceError('SUBMISSION_EFFECT_OUTSIDE_SCOPE')
    # All failed/unknown facts remain intact; binding does not produce pass.
    return record

    package_ref: ImplementationPackageRef
    approval_refs: tuple[ApprovalRef, ...]
    intent_digest: Digest
    evaluated_control_versions: tuple[tuple[ApprovalRef, int], ...]
    evaluator_contract_version: str = 'ordessa.package-binding/1'


def bind_implementation_package(package, grant, *, control_state, control_version, now):
    if type(package) is not ImplementationPackage or type(grant) is not ApprovalGrant:
        raise ReferenceError('INVALID_PACKAGE_BINDING')
    intent = grant.intent
    if type(intent) is not ImplementationAuthorizationIntent:
        raise ReferenceError('ACTION_NOT_AUTHORIZED')
    validate_version(control_version)
    utc_instant(now)
    if control_state != 'granted':
        raise ReferenceError('AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED')
    if not intent.not_before <= now < intent.expires_at:
        raise ReferenceError('AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED')
    p = package.payload
    spec = intent.implementation_spec
    if (package.scope != intent.scope or p.authorization_refs != (grant.ref,)
            or p.change_set != intent.change_set or set(p.design_targets) != set(intent.targets)
            or p.method_ref != intent.method_ref or p.baseline_snapshots != spec.expected_baselines
            or p.implementation_intent_id != spec.implementation_intent_id
            or p.derivation.intent_digest != intent.digest
            or p.acceptance_requirements != spec.acceptance_requirement_refs
            or not set(p.allowed_actions) <= set(intent.actions)
            or set(p.required_review_refs) != set(intent.supporting_review_refs)):
        raise ReferenceError('PACKAGE_GRANT_BINDING_MISMATCH')
    if 'generate_package' not in intent.actions:
        raise ReferenceError('ACTION_NOT_AUTHORIZED')
    scopes = dict(intent.scope_by_action)
    if p.execution_profile_ref not in spec.scope.environment_refs:
        raise ReferenceError('PACKAGE_EXECUTION_PROFILE_MISMATCH')
    for row in p.resolved_file_manifest:
        # File plans are bounded even when the current action merely generates
        # their package; generation never authorizes editing those files.
        path, destination = (row.rename_from, row.path) if row.operation == 'rename' else (row.path, None)
        if not scopes['generate_package'].allows_path(row.repository_id, path, row.operation, destination=destination):
            raise ReferenceError('PACKAGE_SCOPE_MISMATCH')
        if 'edit_repository' in p.allowed_actions and not scopes['edit_repository'].allows_path(
                row.repository_id, path, row.operation, destination=destination):
            raise ReferenceError('PACKAGE_SCOPE_MISMATCH')
    if 'generate_package' not in intent.actions:
        raise ReferenceError('ACTION_NOT_AUTHORIZED')
    return PackageBindingProof(package.ref, (grant.ref,), intent.digest, ((grant.ref, control_version),))

    specs = loaded.manifest.get("documents", [])

            for _, resource in sorted(loaded.resources.items())
            if resource.declaration["kind"] == "document_schema"]

"""Explicit, business-neutral SQLite connection parameters.

The point of this module is to make the *effective* connection contract a
value: every caller that used to hand-write ``sqlite3.connect(...)`` plus a
handful of ``PRAGMA`` statements can instead build one :class:`SQLiteOptions`
and let :func:`ordessa_infrastructure.database.sqlite.create_connection` apply
it. Nothing here owns a schema, a migration, a transaction unit of work or a
store authority.

Design rules (they mirror the task's parameter contract):

* The returned object is a native :class:`sqlite3.Connection`; this module adds
  no wrapper and no connection registry.
* Parameters that Python would default are only passed to ``sqlite3.connect``
  when the caller set them (see :data:`UNSET`). Python 3.12's ``autocommit`` /
  ``isolation_level`` therefore cannot change silently just because a caller
  omitted them: an unset field reproduces plain ``sqlite3.connect`` behaviour.
* ``foreign_keys`` and ``busy_timeout`` are explicit opt-ins. ``None`` means
  "do not touch the connection default"; a value means "apply exactly this".
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable


class _Unset:
    """Sentinel distinguishing "caller did not set this" from ``None``."""

    _instance: "_Unset | None" = None

    def __new__(cls) -> "_Unset":
        if cls._instance is None:
            cls._instance = super().__new__(cls)
        return cls._instance

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - trivial
        return "UNSET"

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return False


#: Marker for "leave this ``sqlite3.connect`` parameter at its Python default".
UNSET = _Unset()


def _is_unset(value: Any) -> bool:
    return value is UNSET


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SQLiteOptions:
    """One caller's explicit connection contract.

    Attributes
    ----------
    location:
        Database file path (or URI when ``uri=True``). Kept as given; callers
        own directory creation so a bare connection helper never creates a
        data root as a side effect.
    uri:
        Forwarded to ``sqlite3.connect``. Default ``False`` keeps the
        historical path-string behaviour.
    timeout:
        Forwarded to ``sqlite3.connect`` as its busy-handler duration. Note
        that ``sqlite3.connect`` also installs ``PRAGMA busy_timeout`` from
        this value; an explicit :attr:`busy_timeout` is applied afterwards and
        therefore wins (see the module README).
    check_same_thread:
        Forwarded to ``sqlite3.connect``. Default ``True`` is the native
        default.
    isolation_level:
        Forwarded only when set. ``None`` selects SQLite autocommit
        (implicit-BEGIN disabled); ``""`` (the native default) keeps implicit
        transactions. Leaving this :data:`UNSET` reproduces the native default.
    autocommit:
        Forwarded only when set (Python 3.12). Leaving this :data:`UNSET`
        reproduces ``sqlite3.LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL``. When not legacy,
        Python ignores ``isolation_level``; both explicitly supplied values
        are forwarded without introducing another transaction policy.
    row_factory:
        Applied after connect when not ``None``. ``None`` means "leave the
        native tuple factory".
    foreign_keys:
        ``True``/``False`` executes exactly that ``PRAGMA foreign_keys``.
        ``None`` leaves the connection's foreign-key setting untouched.
    busy_timeout:
        Milliseconds applied via ``PRAGMA busy_timeout`` when not ``None``.
        Overrides the value ``sqlite3.connect`` derived from ``timeout``.
    """

    location: str | Path
    uri: bool = False
    timeout: float = 5.0
    check_same_thread: bool = True
    isolation_level: Any = field(default=UNSET)
    autocommit: Any = field(default=UNSET)
    row_factory: Callable[..., Any] | None = None
    foreign_keys: bool | None = None
    busy_timeout: int | None = None

    def connect_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The ``sqlite3.connect`` keyword arguments implied by this contract.

        Only explicitly set transaction-control parameters are included, so an
        omitted ``isolation_level``/``autocommit`` cannot alter Python 3.12
        behaviour relative to a plain ``sqlite3.connect`` call.
        """
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
            "timeout": self.timeout,
            "uri": self.uri,
            "check_same_thread": self.check_same_thread,
        }
        if not _is_unset(self.isolation_level):
            kwargs["isolation_level"] = self.isolation_level
        if not _is_unset(self.autocommit):
            kwargs["autocommit"] = self.autocommit
        return kwargs

"""Reusable SQLite connection creation returning a native connection.

This is deliberately *only* connection creation plus the explicit parameter
contract from :mod:`ordessa_infrastructure.database.options`. Business schema,
migrations, repositories, transaction units of work, commit/rollback policy and
WAL timing stay with their existing owners.

Lifecycle contract:

* On any initialisation failure the freshly opened connection is closed and the
  exception propagates, so a caller never receives a half-configured handle.
* On success the returned connection is owned entirely by the caller. A
  ``with connection:`` block is a transaction scope, **not** a close; the
  caller must close it (or hand it to a long-lived owner) explicitly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

from .options import SQLiteOptions

__all__ = ["create_connection", "SQLiteConfigurationError"]


class SQLiteConfigurationError(RuntimeError):
    """A requested connection setting could not actually take effect."""


def _apply_pragma(conn: sqlite3.Connection, statement: str) -> None:
    # ``executescript``/``execute`` run through the same cursor API; using the
    # connection ensures the PRAGMA executes against this handle only.
    conn.execute(statement)


def _apply_foreign_keys(conn: sqlite3.Connection, foreign_keys: bool) -> None:
    """Apply ``PRAGMA foreign_keys`` and prove it took effect.

    ``PRAGMA foreign_keys`` is a silent no-op inside a transaction. In
    particular ``autocommit=False`` starts a connection already inside an
    implicit transaction, so the PRAGMA would leave foreign keys *off* while
    returning success. Reading the value back and refusing a silent mismatch is
    what keeps that combination from handing back an unexpectedly unprotected
    connection.
    """
    wanted = 1 if foreign_keys else 0
    _apply_pragma(conn, "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON" if foreign_keys else "PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF")
    actual = conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys").fetchone()[0]
    if actual != wanted:
        raise SQLiteConfigurationError(
            "PRAGMA foreign_keys did not take effect (requested "
            f"{wanted}, got {actual}); this happens when the connection is "
            "already inside a transaction, e.g. autocommit=False"
        )


def _apply_busy_timeout(conn: sqlite3.Connection, busy_timeout: int) -> None:
    """Apply the requested millisecond value and reject SQLite's silent clamp."""
    wanted = int(busy_timeout)
    _apply_pragma(conn, f"PRAGMA busy_timeout = {wanted}")
    actual = conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout").fetchone()[0]
    if actual != wanted:
        raise SQLiteConfigurationError(
            "PRAGMA busy_timeout did not take effect (requested "
            f"{wanted}, got {actual})"
        )


def create_connection(options: SQLiteOptions) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open one SQLite connection described by ``options``.

    The result is a plain :class:`sqlite3.Connection`. ``options.uri`` selects
    URI handling; ``options.timeout`` and ``options.check_same_thread`` are
    forwarded. ``row_factory``, ``foreign_keys`` and ``busy_timeout`` are
    applied only when the caller asked for them.
    """
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(options.location), **options.connect_kwargs())
    try:
        if options.row_factory is not None:
            conn.row_factory = options.row_factory
        if options.foreign_keys is not None:
            _apply_foreign_keys(conn, options.foreign_keys)
        if options.busy_timeout is not None:
            _apply_busy_timeout(conn, options.busy_timeout)
    except BaseException:
        # Initialisation failed: the new connection is not yet handed over, so
        # closing it is this function's responsibility.
        conn.close()
        raise
    return conn

"""Explicit Python entry-point discovery and metadata, without admission policy.

Import performs no discovery or loading. Enumeration preserves metadata's order
and duplicates; callers own selection and sorting. Loading imports executable
Python code, so the caller must authorize it before calling load_entry_point.
The loaded object is returned unchanged, never invoked or validated here.

Source facts are metadata observations, not proof of the loaded module's origin
or trust. No provider descriptor, factory, registry, context or activation lives
in this module. Python >=3.12 is the distribution's existing runtime boundary.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from importlib import metadata

__all__ = [
    "EntryPointSource",
    "enumerate_entry_points",
    "entry_point_source",
    "load_entry_point",
]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EntryPointSource:
    """Optional source metadata; errors never imply admission or rejection.

    group/name/value identify the declared entry point. Distribution name and
    version describe its attached distribution, not the object imported under
    the current sys.path. Missing attributes stay None. Failed or non-text
    attributes stay None and are identified in metadata_errors; independent
    available fields are retained. Error strings contain field and error type,
    without invoking arbitrary exception formatting.
    """

    group: str | None
    name: str | None
    value: str | None
    distribution_name: str | None = None
    distribution_version: str | None = None
    metadata_errors: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def enumerate_entry_points(group: str) -> tuple[metadata.EntryPoint, ...]:
    """Enumerate exactly group, without loading, normalizing or sorting it.

    Metadata discovery exceptions propagate unchanged. The caller may supply
    already-selected entry points to its own loader instead of enumerating.
    """
    if not isinstance(group, str):
        raise TypeError("entry-point group must be a string")
    if not group:
        raise ValueError("entry-point group must be non-empty")
    return tuple(metadata.entry_points().select(group=group))


def _optional_text(owner, attribute: str, label: str, errors: list[str]) -> str | None:
    try:
        value = getattr(owner, attribute, None)
    except Exception as exc:
        errors.append(f"{label}: {type(exc).__name__}")
        return None
    if value is None or isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    errors.append(f"{label}: TypeError")
    return None


def entry_point_source(entry_point: metadata.EntryPoint) -> EntryPointSource:
    """Observe one entry point's optional metadata without loading its target."""
    errors: list[str] = []
    group = _optional_text(entry_point, "group", "group", errors)
    name = _optional_text(entry_point, "name", "name", errors)
    value = _optional_text(entry_point, "value", "value", errors)
    try:
        distribution = getattr(entry_point, "dist", None)
    except Exception as exc:
        errors.append(f"distribution: {type(exc).__name__}")
        distribution = None
    distribution_name = _optional_text(distribution, "name", "distribution_name", errors)
    distribution_version = _optional_text(distribution, "version", "distribution_version", errors)
    return EntryPointSource(
        group, name, value, distribution_name, distribution_version, tuple(errors)
    )


def load_entry_point(entry_point: metadata.EntryPoint) -> object:
    """Explicitly load once, return unchanged; native errors propagate.

    This does not call factories, descriptor/build methods or provider runtime,
    and neither enumerates nor retries an alternative entry point on failure.
    """
    return entry_point.load()

"""Content-addressed immutable object publication."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from ..encoding.digests import sha256
import os
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ObjectRecord:
    digest: str
    size: int
    path: Path


class ObjectStore:
    """Content-addressed bytes at an explicit root; no product layout.

    The two-character SHA256 shard, digest and ObjectRecord format, corruption
    errors and file fsync/replace sequence retain the original mechanism. This
    is not the Engineering BlobStore authority or a record-format validator.
    It does not add a directory-fsync or no-clobber guarantee. Temporary cleanup
    retains the original path-based behavior and requires trusted namespace
    control; it is not asserted race-free against arbitrary same-UID mutation.
    """

    def __init__(self, storage_root: Path | str) -> None:
        self.root = Path(storage_root).resolve()

    def path_for(self, digest: str) -> Path:
        if (not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest.startswith("sha256:")
                or len(digest) != 71
                or any(character not in "0123456789abcdef" for character in digest[7:])):
            raise ValueError("invalid object digest")
        value = digest[7:]
        return self.root / value[:2] / value

    def publish(self, content: bytes) -> ObjectRecord:
        digest = "sha256:" + sha256(content).hex()
        target = self.path_for(digest)
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if target.exists():
            existing = target.read_bytes()
            if sha256(existing) != sha256(content):
                raise IOError("existing immutable object failed digest verification")
            return ObjectRecord(digest, len(content), target)
        fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="publish-", dir=target.parent)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
                stream.write(content)
                stream.flush()
                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
            os.replace(temporary, target)
            if target.read_bytes() != content:
                raise IOError("published immutable object failed verification")
        finally:
            try:
                os.unlink(temporary)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        return ObjectRecord(digest, len(content), target)

    def read(self, digest: str) -> bytes:
        content = self.path_for(digest).read_bytes()
        actual = "sha256:" + sha256(content).hex()
        if actual != digest:
            raise IOError("immutable object digest mismatch")
        return content

__all__ = ["ObjectRecord", "ObjectStore"]

"""Directory-descriptor traversal relative to a trusted root descriptor.

Capabilities:

* :func:`open_directory_relative` opens one child directory of a trusted
  directory fd, refusing absolute names, separators and ``..``.
* :func:`open_directory_absolute` walks an absolute path one component at a
  time from ``/``, so no intermediate name is resolved through a symlink it
  should not follow.
* :func:`open_directory_nofollow` opens a directory path without following a
  final symlink and refuses when the directory identity (device/inode) changed
  between the ``lstat`` check and the open.

Ownership rules, stated once and relied on everywhere:

* A *borrowed* descriptor (the trusted parent/root fd passed in) is never
  closed here.
* Every descriptor this module opens is returned to the caller, who owns it.
  If an internal step fails, the newly opened descriptor is closed before the
  exception propagates, so a failure never leaks an fd.
* ``O_NOFOLLOW`` (and ``O_DIRECTORY`` for directory opens) is required. Where
  the platform cannot supply the guarantee the call refuses with
  :class:`PlatformUnsupportedError`; it never substitutes ``0``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import errno
import os
import stat
from pathlib import Path

from .errors import (
    DirectoryReplacedError,
    PlatformUnsupportedError,
    UnsafeFileTypeError,
    UnsafePathError,
)

__all__ = [
    "open_directory_relative",
    "open_directory_absolute",
    "open_directory_nofollow",
    "is_safe_component",
]


def is_safe_component(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when ``name`` is a single, non-traversing path component."""
    return (
        isinstance(name, str)
        and name not in {"", ".", ".."}
        and "\x00" not in name
        and "/" not in name
        and "\\" not in name
        and os.sep not in name
        and not os.path.isabs(name)
    )


def require_nofollow() -> int:
    """Return ``O_NOFOLLOW`` or refuse; never fall back to ``0``."""
    flag = getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", None)
    if not flag:
        raise PlatformUnsupportedError(
            "O_NOFOLLOW is unavailable; refusing to open without the symlink guarantee"
        )
    return flag


def _directory_flags() -> int:
    nofollow = require_nofollow()
    directory = getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", None)
    if not directory:
        raise PlatformUnsupportedError(
            "O_DIRECTORY is unavailable; refusing to open without the directory guarantee"
        )
    return os.O_RDONLY | directory | nofollow | getattr(os, "O_CLOEXEC", 0)


def open_directory_relative(parent_fd: int, name: str) -> int:
    """Open directory ``name`` under a trusted ``parent_fd`` and return the fd.

    ``parent_fd`` is borrowed and not closed. The returned fd is newly opened
    and owned by the caller.
    """
    if not is_safe_component(name):
        raise UnsafePathError(f"unsafe directory component: {name!r}")
    flags = _directory_flags()
    try:
        fd = os.open(name, flags, dir_fd=parent_fd)
    except OSError as exc:
        if exc.errno == errno.ELOOP:
            raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"symlink refused: {name!r}") from exc
        raise
    try:
        if not stat.S_ISDIR(os.fstat(fd).st_mode):
            raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"not a directory: {name!r}")
    except BaseException:
        os.close(fd)
        raise
    return fd


def open_directory_absolute(path: str | Path) -> int:
    """Open an absolute directory by walking it from ``/`` component by component.

    Refuses ``..`` components and separator-bearing names. ``path`` is made
    absolute lexically; each component is opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW`` relative
    to the previously opened directory. The caller owns the returned fd.
    """
    absolute = Path(path).absolute()
    parts = absolute.parts
    if not absolute.is_absolute() or not parts or parts[0] != os.sep:
        raise UnsafePathError(f"path is not absolute: {path!r}")
    flags = _directory_flags()
    fd = os.open(os.sep, flags)
    try:
        for part in parts[1:]:
            if not is_safe_component(part):
                raise UnsafePathError(f"unsafe directory component: {part!r}")
            try:
                nxt = os.open(part, flags, dir_fd=fd)
            except OSError as exc:
                if exc.errno == errno.ELOOP:
                    raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"symlink refused: {part!r}") from exc
                raise
            os.close(fd)
            fd = nxt
            if not stat.S_ISDIR(os.fstat(fd).st_mode):
                raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"not a directory: {part!r}")
    except BaseException:
        os.close(fd)
        raise
    return fd


def open_directory_nofollow(path: str | Path) -> int:
    """Open directory ``path`` refusing a symlink and a replaced identity.

    The pre-open ``lstat`` establishes the expected ``(st_dev, st_ino)``; the
    post-open ``fstat`` must match, otherwise the directory was replaced
    between check and open and :class:`DirectoryReplacedError` is raised. The
    caller owns the returned fd.
    """
    target = Path(path)
    info = target.lstat()
    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
        raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"unsafe directory: {path!r}")
    fd = os.open(target, _directory_flags())
    try:
        actual = os.fstat(fd)
        if not stat.S_ISDIR(actual.st_mode) or (actual.st_dev, actual.st_ino) != (info.st_dev, info.st_ino):
            raise DirectoryReplacedError(f"directory was replaced: {path!r}")
    except BaseException:
        os.close(fd)
        raise
    return fd

"""Neutral filesystem mechanism errors.

These are intentionally free of any business error code. Owners that need their
own vocabulary (for example Engineering's ``package_directory_unsafe``) catch
these and re-raise their own errors, so the mechanism never leaks a product
contract and never invents a second authority over the caller's policy.
"""
from __future__ import annotations


class FilesystemMechanismError(Exception):
    """Base class for every error raised by this package."""


class UnsafePathError(FilesystemMechanismError):
    """A path component was absolute, empty, ``.``/``..`` or separator-bearing."""


class UnsafeFileTypeError(FilesystemMechanismError):
    """An object was a symlink, or not the directory/regular file required."""


class DirectoryReplacedError(FilesystemMechanismError):
    """A directory's identity changed between check and open."""


class PlatformUnsupportedError(FilesystemMechanismError):
    """The platform lacks the required guarantee (``O_NOFOLLOW``/``O_DIRECTORY``).

    Raised instead of silently reading/creating a symlink-followable object.
    A caller may catch this and refuse, but the mechanism never falls back to
    ``O_NOFOLLOW = 0`` and pretends the guarantee held.
    """


class FileAlreadyExistsError(FilesystemMechanismError):
    """Exclusive creation found an existing name (``O_EXCL``)."""


class PublicationError(FilesystemMechanismError):
    """A staged single-file publication failed.

    ``stage`` names the stage that failed and ``target_may_have_changed`` is
    true when the atomic replace had already completed, so the caller must not
    assume the previous target content is intact. This mechanism never rolls
    back and never deletes the final target on the caller's behalf.
    """

    def __init__(self, stage: str, message: str, *, target_may_have_changed: bool = False) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.stage = stage
        self.target_may_have_changed = target_may_have_changed

Every open is made relative to a trusted directory descriptor with

* The borrowed ``directory_fd`` is never closed here.
* A returned file descriptor is owned by the caller.
* ``O_NOFOLLOW`` is mandatory. Where the platform lacks it the call refuses
  with :class:`PlatformUnsupportedError`; it never pretends ``0`` is safe.
* Permission bits are always passed in by the caller; this module never
  forces one business mode onto every file.

import errno
import os
import stat

from .directories import is_safe_component, require_nofollow
from .errors import (

    PlatformUnsupportedError,
    UnsafeFileTypeError,
    UnsafePathError,

def _base_flags() -> int:
    # ``O_NONBLOCK`` is added so opening a FIFO/device never blocks before the
    # post-open type check can reject it. For a regular file it has no effect
    # on reads/writes.
    return require_nofollow() | getattr(os, "O_CLOEXEC", 0) | getattr(os, "O_NONBLOCK", 0)


def _check_component(name: str) -> None:
    if not is_safe_component(name):
        raise UnsafePathError(f"unsafe file component: {name!r}")


def open_file_at(
    directory_fd: int,
    name: str,
    flags: int,
    *,
    mode: int = 0o600,
    expected_mode: int | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Open ``name`` under ``directory_fd`` and return a caller-owned fd.

    ``O_NOFOLLOW`` is always added. A non-regular resulting file is refused and
    the fd closed. When ``expected_mode`` is given the opened inode's
    permission bits must match exactly.
    """
    _check_component(name)
    try:
        fd = os.open(name, flags | _base_flags(), mode, dir_fd=directory_fd)
    except OSError as exc:
        if exc.errno == errno.ELOOP:
            raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"symlink refused: {name!r}") from exc
        raise
    try:
        info = os.fstat(fd)
        if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
            raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"not a regular file: {name!r}")
        if expected_mode is not None and stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) != expected_mode:
            raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"unexpected file mode for {name!r}")
    except BaseException:
        os.close(fd)
        raise
    return fd


def open_regular_at(directory_fd: int, name: str, *, expected_mode: int | None = None) -> int:
    """Read-only regular-file open under ``directory_fd``."""
    return open_file_at(directory_fd, name, os.O_RDONLY, mode=0, expected_mode=expected_mode)


def read_regular_at(directory_fd: int, name: str, *, limit: int | None = None) -> bytes:
    """Read the bytes of a regular file under ``directory_fd``.

    ``limit`` bounds the accepted size in bytes. The bound is enforced twice:
    once on the opened size and again on the accumulated bytes actually read,
    so a file that grows after the open cannot slip past the limit. A file that
    exceeds the limit raises :class:`UnsafeFileTypeError` rather than returning
    partial data.
    """
    fd = open_regular_at(directory_fd, name)
    try:
        if limit is not None and os.fstat(fd).st_size > limit:
            raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"file exceeds limit: {name!r}")
        chunks: list[bytes] = []
        size = 0
        while True:
            want = 1 << 16
            if limit is not None:
                want = min(want, limit + 1 - size)
                if want <= 0:
                    raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"file exceeds limit: {name!r}")
            chunk = os.read(fd, want)
            if not chunk:
                break
            size += len(chunk)
            if limit is not None and size > limit:
                raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"file exceeds limit: {name!r}")
            chunks.append(chunk)
        return b"".join(chunks)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def create_exclusive_at(directory_fd: int, name: str, *, mode: int, flags: int = 0) -> int:
    """Exclusively create a new regular file and return a caller-owned fd.

    Combines ``O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW`` with any extra
    ``flags`` (for example ``O_APPEND``). ``mode`` is required and used
    verbatim. An existing name is reported as :class:`FileAlreadyExistsError`.
    """
    _check_component(name)
    open_flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | flags | _base_flags()
    try:
        fd = os.open(name, open_flags, mode, dir_fd=directory_fd)
    except OSError as exc:
        if exc.errno == errno.EEXIST:
            raise FileAlreadyExistsError(f"already exists: {name!r}") from exc
        if exc.errno == errno.ELOOP:
            raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"symlink refused: {name!r}") from exc
        raise
    try:
        if not stat.S_ISREG(os.fstat(fd).st_mode):
            raise UnsafeFileTypeError(f"not a regular file: {name!r}")
    except BaseException:
        os.close(fd)
        raise
    return fd


def sync_directory(directory_fd: int) -> None:
    """Flush a directory's entries; the caller decides when this is required."""
    os.fsync(directory_fd)

"""Staged single-file publication with honest durability accounting.

A publication runs four explicit stages:

1. ``write``           — create the temporary file exclusively and write bytes.
2. ``file_fsync``      — ``fsync`` the temporary file's bytes.
3. ``replace``         — atomically rename the temporary file onto the target.
4. ``directory_fsync`` — ``fsync`` the parent directory so the rename is durable.

Semantics: the target is **replaced atomically** (POSIX ``rename`` overwrites).
There is no "do not overwrite" mode; if a caller needs no-clobber it must prove
absence itself, because a portable, race-free no-clobber publication is not what
this primitive offers.

The stage boundary matters. Once the replace succeeds the target has *already
changed*; if the directory ``fsync`` then fails, persistence is unknown. This
module therefore:

* does **not** roll back the replace,
* does **not** delete the final target,
* reports :class:`PublicationError` with ``stage='directory_fsync'`` and
  ``target_may_have_changed=True``.

Before the replace, a failure leaves the target untouched and closes the owned
file descriptor, but does not unlink the temporary name. A pathname identity
check followed by unlink cannot safely exclude a concurrent replacement. The
temporary may therefore remain complete, partial or empty; callers own its
cleanup under conditions that exclude concurrent namespace changes. This
function never deletes a replacement file or performs an implicit retry.

Success still uses a pathname rename. Callers must control ``temp_name`` until
the rename completes; this primitive does not fence another actor replacing the
source name or attest that the renamed inode is the one opened for writing.

Complete-directory publication, business validation, identity-change cleanup,
``wal``/``shm`` cleanup and record-format specific commits stay with their
owners; this is deliberately a single-file primitive.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum

from .directories import is_safe_component
from .errors import PublicationError, UnsafePathError
from .files import create_exclusive_at, sync_directory

__all__ = ["PublicationStage", "PublishedFile", "publish_file"]


class PublicationStage(str, Enum):
    WRITE = "write"
    FILE_FSYNC = "file_fsync"
    REPLACE = "replace"
    DIRECTORY_FSYNC = "directory_fsync"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PublishedFile:
    """Outcome of a completed publication (all four stages succeeded)."""

    target: str
    temp: str


def _validate_names(target_name: str, temp_name: str) -> None:
    """Reject unsafe or ambiguous names before any create/write happens."""
    if not is_safe_component(target_name):
        raise UnsafePathError(f"unsafe target name: {target_name!r}")
    if not is_safe_component(temp_name):
        raise UnsafePathError(f"unsafe temp name: {temp_name!r}")
    if target_name == temp_name:
        raise ValueError("temp_name must differ from target_name")


def _write_all(fd: int, data: bytes) -> None:
    view = memoryview(data)
    while view:
        written = os.write(fd, view)
        if not written:
            # A zero-byte write must never spin forever.
            raise OSError("short write while publishing")
        view = view[written:]


def publish_file(
    directory_fd: int,
    target_name: str,
    data: bytes,
    *,
    temp_name: str,
    mode: int = 0o600,
) -> PublishedFile:
    """Publish ``data`` as ``target_name`` inside ``directory_fd``.

    ``target_name`` and ``temp_name`` must be distinct safe components; both are
    validated before any file is created. ``mode`` is the caller's explicit
    permission for the new file (the target keeps the temporary's mode).
    Before replacement, failures may leave ``temp_name`` behind. This function
    closes its fd but never removes that name; safe cleanup is the caller's
    responsibility. Retrying the same name will refuse while it remains present.
    """
    _validate_names(target_name, temp_name)

    fd = None
    try:
        try:
            fd = create_exclusive_at(directory_fd, temp_name, mode=mode)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised as a staged error
            raise PublicationError(PublicationStage.WRITE.value, f"temp create failed: {temp_name!r}") from exc
        try:
            _write_all(fd, data)
        except BaseException as exc:
            raise PublicationError(PublicationStage.WRITE.value, "writing temp failed") from exc
        try:
            os.fsync(fd)
        except BaseException as exc:
            raise PublicationError(PublicationStage.FILE_FSYNC.value, "file fsync failed") from exc
    finally:
        if fd is not None:
            os.close(fd)

    try:
        os.rename(temp_name, target_name, src_dir_fd=directory_fd, dst_dir_fd=directory_fd)
    except BaseException as exc:
        # Replace did not happen: the previous target is intact.
        raise PublicationError(PublicationStage.REPLACE.value, "atomic replace failed") from exc

    try:
        sync_directory(directory_fd)
    except BaseException as exc:
        # The target has already changed. Durability is unknown. No rollback,
        # no deletion of the final file.
        raise PublicationError(
            PublicationStage.DIRECTORY_FSYNC.value,
            "directory fsync failed after replace; target may have changed",
            target_may_have_changed=True,
        ) from exc

    return PublishedFile(target=target_name, temp=temp_name)

"""Stable opaque opaque identifiers and record timestamps."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Mapping
from uuid import uuid4

__all__ = ["now", "opaque_id", "RequestKey"]

_LOCAL_ID = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$")
_PRINCIPAL_SCOPE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$")


def now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def opaque_id(prefix: str) -> str:
    return f"{prefix}_{uuid4().hex}"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RequestKey:
    """Opaque idempotency partition and request key.

    These historical field names do not authenticate a principal, verify an
    Environment lifecycle or namespace owner, or grant permission. The
    ``comparison`` payload is caller-provided comparison data; this technical
    value does not interpret it as a binding, guarantee, or target. It carries
    no business references.
    """

    environment_namespace: str
    principal_scope: str
    request_id: str
    comparison: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict, compare=True)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not isinstance(self.environment_namespace, str) or not _LOCAL_ID.match(self.environment_namespace):
            raise ValueError(
                f"RequestKey.environment_namespace must match { _LOCAL_ID.pattern!r}: "
                f"{self.environment_namespace!r}"
            )
        if not isinstance(self.principal_scope, str) or not _PRINCIPAL_SCOPE.match(self.principal_scope):
            raise ValueError("RequestKey.principal_scope is malformed")
        if not isinstance(self.request_id, str) or not _LOCAL_ID.match(self.request_id):
            raise ValueError(
                f"RequestKey.request_id must match { _LOCAL_ID.pattern!r}: {self.request_id!r}"
            )

"""Secret-store contract; bytes and persisted locator meanings unchanged."""
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Protocol

MAX_SECRET_BYTES = 1024 * 1024


class SecretStore(Protocol):
    def import_file(self, source: Path, kind: str) -> tuple[str, str]: ...
    def read(self, locator: str) -> bytes: ...
    def delete(self, locator: str) -> None: ...


class SecretLocatorUnavailable(RuntimeError):
    """A recorded credential's locator is not resolvable in the store.

    Typed (``code = CREDENTIAL_NOT_AVAILABLE``) so ``_safe_code`` surfaces it as
    the execution reason instead of a reasonless ``EXECUTION_FAILED``. The
    message carries only the non-sensitive locator id and why it cannot be read;
    no secret bytes are ever included.
    """

    code = "CREDENTIAL_NOT_AVAILABLE"

    def __init__(self, locator: str) -> None:
        self.locator = locator
        super().__init__(
            f"credential locator {locator!r} is not available on this machine "
            "(the credential was never imported here, or was removed); "
            "select a profile whose credential is present")



__all__ = ["SecretStore", "MAX_SECRET_BYTES", "SecretLocatorUnavailable"]

"""Windows current-user DPAPI store for explicitly imported credential bytes."""
from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
from ctypes import wintypes
import csv
import io
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
from uuid import uuid4


from .secrets import MAX_SECRET_BYTES


class _Blob(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("cbData", wintypes.DWORD), ("pbData", ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_byte))]


def _blob(content: bytes) -> tuple[_Blob, object]:
    buffer = ctypes.create_string_buffer(content)
    return _Blob(len(content), ctypes.cast(buffer, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_byte))), buffer


def _dpapi_functions():
    crypt32 = ctypes.WinDLL("crypt32", use_last_error=True)
    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    arguments = [
        ctypes.POINTER(_Blob), wintypes.LPCWSTR, ctypes.POINTER(_Blob),
        ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, wintypes.DWORD, ctypes.POINTER(_Blob),
    ]
    crypt32.CryptProtectData.argtypes = arguments
    crypt32.CryptProtectData.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    crypt32.CryptUnprotectData.argtypes = [
        ctypes.POINTER(_Blob), ctypes.POINTER(wintypes.LPWSTR), ctypes.POINTER(_Blob),
        ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, wintypes.DWORD, ctypes.POINTER(_Blob),
    ]
    crypt32.CryptUnprotectData.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    kernel32.LocalFree.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
    kernel32.LocalFree.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
    return crypt32, kernel32


class WindowsDpapiSecretStore:
    """Native current-user DPAPI; root and description are supplied by caller.

    Construction does not provision directories. Import/read/delete retain the
    original .dpapi bytes, credential_ locator, bounds, ACL and error behavior.
    No Linux backend, product layout or plaintext fallback is selected here.
    """

    def __init__(self, storage_root: Path | str, *, protect_description: str) -> None:
        if os.name != "nt":
            raise RuntimeError("SECRET_STORE_WINDOWS_REQUIRED")
        self.root = Path(storage_root).resolve()
        self._protect_description = protect_description

    def import_file(self, source: Path, kind: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        del kind
        if source.is_symlink() or not source.is_file():
            raise ValueError("CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_INVALID")
        source = source.resolve(strict=True)
        size = source.stat().st_size
        if size <= 0 or size > MAX_SECRET_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_OUTSIDE_BOUND")
        content = source.read_bytes()
        try:
            protected = self._protect(content)
        finally:
            content = b""
        credential_id = f"credential_{uuid4().hex}"
        locator = f"{credential_id}.dpapi"
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._protect_acl(self.root)
        target = self.root / locator
        fd = os.open(target, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
            stream.write(protected)
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        self._protect_acl(target)
        return credential_id, locator

    def read(self, locator: str) -> bytes:
        if not locator.endswith(".dpapi") or Path(locator).name != locator:
            raise ValueError("CREDENTIAL_LOCATOR_INVALID")
        path = self.root / locator
        if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size > MAX_SECRET_BYTES * 2:
            raise ValueError("CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE")
        return self._unprotect(path.read_bytes())

    def delete(self, locator: str) -> None:
        if not locator.endswith(".dpapi") or Path(locator).name != locator:
            raise ValueError("CREDENTIAL_LOCATOR_INVALID")
        path = self.root / locator
        if path.exists():
            path.unlink()

    def _protect(self, content: bytes) -> bytes:
        source, source_buffer = _blob(content)
        output = _Blob()
        crypt32, kernel32 = _dpapi_functions()
        if not crypt32.CryptProtectData(
            ctypes.byref(source), self._protect_description, None, None, None,
            0x01, ctypes.byref(output),
        ):
            raise ctypes.WinError()
        try:
            return ctypes.string_at(output.pbData, output.cbData)
        finally:
            kernel32.LocalFree(ctypes.cast(output.pbData, ctypes.c_void_p))
            del source_buffer

    @staticmethod
    def _unprotect(content: bytes) -> bytes:
        source, source_buffer = _blob(content)
        output = _Blob()
        crypt32, kernel32 = _dpapi_functions()
        if not crypt32.CryptUnprotectData(
            ctypes.byref(source), None, None, None, None, 0x01, ctypes.byref(output),
        ):
            raise ctypes.WinError()
        try:
            return ctypes.string_at(output.pbData, output.cbData)
        finally:
            kernel32.LocalFree(ctypes.cast(output.pbData, ctypes.c_void_p))
            del source_buffer

    @staticmethod
    def _protect_acl(path: Path) -> None:
        identity = subprocess.run(
            ["whoami.exe", "/user", "/fo", "csv", "/nh"],
            check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
        ).stdout
        fields = next(csv.reader(io.StringIO(identity)))
        if len(fields) < 2 or not fields[1].startswith("S-"):
            raise RuntimeError("WINDOWS_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE")
        subprocess.run(
            ["icacls.exe", str(path), "/inheritance:r", "/grant:r", f"*{fields[1]}:(F)"],
            check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
        )

__all__ = ["WindowsDpapiSecretStore"]
